description: Required test evidence for the four attested G0 checks. Each entry names one executed test, the rule mode it covers, the expected result in words, and the official basis for that expectation. scripts/m8_evidence.py derives the checks-file booleans from a real test run against this list; a missing, failed or renamed test makes the corresponding check false instead of silently passing.

basis_references.rules_p8: 2016 Revised rulebook p.8: farm expansion, stables, pastures and fencing
basis_references.rules_p10: 2016 Revised rulebook p.10: baking and food conversion
basis_references.rules_p12: 2016 Revised rulebook p.12: component limits (family 5, stables 4, fences 15)
basis_references.appendix_p2: 2016 Revised appendix p.2: the ten major improvements, their costs, scores and conversion rates
basis_references.appendix_p7_8: 2016 Revised appendix p.7-8: fencing, optional/compulsory action parts, the two-player additional action tiles
basis_references.appendix_p11_12: 2016 Revised appendix p.11-12: scoring categories, leftover-resource bonus and beggar cards

m8_rule_evidence.summary: Official-rule expected-result tests. A passing run of this list is evidence that the documented expectations still hold; it is not a proof over the whole state space.

tests.expectation: 0-1 fields score -1, 2 fields 1, 3 fields 2, and a field with a remaining crop still counts as a field
a clay oven converts exactly one grain into five food per bake; asking for three is rejected atomically
a stone oven converts at most two grain into four food each; a third grain is rejected
a cooking hearth converts one vegetable into three food as a free action
the animal market cattle transaction costs one food, and an unaffordable attempt leaves the state unchanged
all ten major improvements charge their documented cost and award their documented score
the three workshops award the documented leftover-resource bonus tiers
harvests occur after rounds 4, 7, 9, 11, 13 and 14 only
the first field and the first animal score -1, and the zero cases score 0
the tie-break compares only unspent wood, clay, reed and stone
the two-player animal market offers three distinct transactions with their documented costs
the two-player resource market provides stone and food and never reed
wood accumulated on the copse is kept when another additional tile is used
the additional family-growth tile is available only from round five with a free room
renovation upgrades every room and costs one reed in addition to the per-room material
a used or unrevealed space is never offered and is rejected when forced

m8_legal_api_evidence.summary: The legal-detail API accepts legal details that the default policy never proposes and rejects illegal ones without mutating state. SimpleDetails is a policy, not the definition of the legal action set.

tests.expectation: a two-cell pasture that SimpleDetails never proposes is validated and applied, charging six fence segments
a fence layout that overlaps a room is rejected and the state hash is unchanged
a detail-bearing space without a detail, and an unrevealed space, are both rejected atomically
human input and the AI detail policy pass the same validator, and a deliberately illegal variant fails it
the staged hint API exposes the legal elementary parameters for a detail-bearing space
the hint payload contains only the acting player's own hand and public information
the web view exposes the staged hints and the available spaces for the same state
a plow cell other than the default policy's first empty cell is validated and applied
plowing a room cell is rejected and leaves the state unchanged
a sowing layout that puts the vegetable before the grain is accepted, although the default policy would sow grain first
sowing the same field twice, or a room cell, is rejected atomically
placing both sheep in stables instead of the pet and the pasture is accepted when capacity allows
two sheep in one stable is rejected and the state is unchanged

evaluation_observation_noninterference.summary: A change to hidden state (opponent hand order or identity, unrevealed round order, internal RNG) must not change the acting player's public observation.

tests.expectation: reordering or substituting the opponent's hidden cards changes the state hash but not the own observation
changing unrevealed round order or the internal RNG state does not change the public observation
the observation carries only public fields plus the acting player's own hand

evaluation_ci_reproducible.summary: The same seed and policies reproduce the same evaluation game, and the committed log replays to the same final state.

tests.expectation: three seeds reproduce identical actions, final hash, scores and ranks with the additional tile off and on
two seeds reproduce identical four-player games
the seeded card deal reproduces the same game and the card log replays with the same card set
different seeds produce different final states, so a seed really selects the game
identical seed and policies give identical hashes, scores and ranks for both comparison arms
simulation-count MCTS replays the same action log and final state for the same seed
100 seeded games per additional-tile setting replay and round-trip through save/load
